quest.title: The Dust Settles
quest.description: The hiding place of the infamous bounty target and criminal, Hark, the Crackjaw, appears to have been uncovered...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Nefer and Jahoda! What are you two doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Working, of course! We finally found a lead on our unresolved bounty.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jahoda tells you all about the bounty target, Hark the "Crackjaw," as well as all the info the Curatorium of Secrets has been able to collect...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's start with our conclusion: The real hermit, Derwent, is likely dead, and the man living in his hut is the bounty target, Hark, the Crackjaw.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The diary scraps Jahoda uncovered are enough to show that even though Derwent knew who he was, he still took him in.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It shouldn't come as a shock that Hark has returned to his old ways. After dispatching Derwent, he took over the hermit's identity.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: When I went to investigate, he wouldn't show his face, but no matter how you look at it, there's no way the man in that hut was the real Derwent.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Taking on the role of a hermit also means Hark can get up to all sorts of bizarre activities without arousing any real suspicion. The mask he wears clearly has nothing to do with "self-cultivation" — he's wearing it to hide his scar!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As for the missing merchant, the worst-case scenario is that he's already dead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can someone be so... evil!? Repaying others' kindness with murder... It makes Paimon's blood boil!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: For what it's worth, I don't think Hark stole those goods from the Peripatetic Circle — not enough motive.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He'd behaved himself well enough for 10 whole years. Is the price of a few stolen goods really enough to make him throw away everything he'd worked for? I don't believe so.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, let's indulge in a little speculation.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We already know that he returned to the wreckage of the Atlas and attacked the treasure hunters who came looking for treasure. When people are in dire straits, they often instinctively return to where it all began.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: When he was still the helmsman on the Atlas, he had fame, wealth — everything he wanted. But what about once he joined the Peripatetic Circle?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Even after 10 years of good behavior, the second something was stolen, everyone turned their suspicion onto him.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What must have stung even more — Juhani, who was once a pirate, albeit one of significantly less renown, remained free from suspicion.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He accused Juhani there and then, but no one believed him.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Driven by disappointment and rage, he made his first mistake. That was the turning point.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Whatever went down in that hermit's hut was likely a similar situation... For someone like that, even the smallest of conflicts can blow up into a fatal confrontation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}. We can't allow someone as dangerous as that to keep walking around doing bad stuff!

choices.text: Let me deal with this dangerous criminal!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #Since {NICKNAME} is so eager, you should get some rest, Jahoda.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Alright, I've been working overtime on this investigation, I think I deserve a holiday!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: As for whether my speculations are correct, we'll find out soon enough.

choices.text: Bounty or no, let me deal with this!

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: ...I've not done anything to any of you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It sounds like you already know why we're here.

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: ...All of that stuff's in the past. I just want to live a peaceful life.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: A life made from stealing someone else's place? First Juhani, but that didn't work, so now Derwent.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Poor performances never fool the audience for long. There won't be any more victims.

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: ...Juhani? You're saying I took *his* place?

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: It was never his to take! Everything he had, he got by looking nicer, talking nicer.

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: We were the same! Everything he took — it belonged to me!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: And what about Mr. Derwent and the merchant? What did they do to you?

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: They... They asked questions they shouldn't have asked. Just like you...

dialogues.speaker: Derwent?
dialogues.text: So die!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As expected — just another pathetic soul who can't stop repeating the same mistakes. I have to say, I'm a little disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He stopped himself from doing wrong for so many years, but in the end... Does this mean bad people can't mend their ways?

choices.text: It's harder to keep doing good.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Every decision was his to make. Even just now, he could have chosen to admit his mistakes. But he chose violence instead.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Every move was poorly made, and every one led him to this end.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #But enough about him. Here's to a job well done. {NICKNAME}, you can take the bounty proof to Leszek, as arranged.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: It was great to have you two take the reins! I could've sworn I was on a vacation today!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Hehe, and now that it's over, I think it's about time to get started on your next job, right, Jahoda?
